leadIn:
I’m using the active settle workflow: I’ll first trace the export/data flow and its tests, then bring only genuinely user-owned behavior choices to the native question form before changing code.

This is a **bounded** change: the existing export flow already owns caching in `src/exporter.js` and `src/cache.js`.

Verified facts:

- `src/cache.js` accepts cached rows for six hours based only on `writtenAt`.
- `src/store.js` reads `data/orders.json`, which the README says is rewritten roughly every 15 minutes.
- `src/exporter.js` keys cache entries only by date range, so an upstream rewrite cannot invalidate an existing entry.
- `README.md` says the nightly batch needs caching for its 10-minute window, while the exact freshness contract for ad hoc runs is explicitly undecided.

**Inference:** this explains the stale exports, but the repository does not authorize whether freshness should follow source rewrites everywhere or only for interactive usage. That choice determines the cache contract, concurrency behavior, CLI surface, and tests.

questions.question: When `data/orders.json` changes, when should an export reflect it? A wrong choice either preserves stale finance output or risks the nightly performance target; the six-hour cache in `src/cache.js` currently ignores rewrites documented in `README.md`.

options.label: On source change (Recommended)
options.description: Invalidate matching cached results after an orders-file rewrite for all runs; adds a cheap source metadata check and may retry if the file changes during export.

options.label: Ad hoc only
options.description: Make interactive runs fresh while preserving nightly staleness, but requires a new mode/flag and changes the CLI contract.

options.label: Shorter TTL
options.description: Bound staleness by time without tracking rewrites, but can still serve stale data and may reduce nightly cache effectiveness.

leadIn:
The first decision settles the outcome: ad hoc exports must refresh after an upstream rewrite, while nightly runs may reuse day-old data.

Verified facts:

- `src/cli.js` currently exposes only two positional dates; there is no way to identify an ad hoc or nightly invocation.
- `README.md` says the external nightly script is not in this repository, so reportkit cannot infer its caller reliably.
- `src/store.js` reads and parses the live file synchronously; malformed or half-written JSON currently fails the command.
- Cache files persist under `.reportkit-cache`; no repository job mutates them except reportkit itself.

**Open tension:** one explicit CLI mode is required, and the default decides whether existing callers gain freshness automatically or retain compatibility. The source can also be rewritten during a run, so we must settle whether a fresh export completes from one snapshot or retries. These answers determine the public CLI contract and recovery tests.

questions.question: How should callers select the freshness policy? A wrong default either leaves unchanged ad hoc commands stale or changes nightly behavior; `src/cli.js` currently accepts only `<from> <to>` and the nightly caller is external.

options.label: Fresh default (Recommended)
options.description: Existing ad hoc commands become fresh and nightly adds `--allow-stale`; the external nightly script must be updated.

options.label: Fresh flag
options.description: Preserve all existing calls and add `--fresh`; finance must opt in every time, so accidental stale ad hoc exports remain possible.

questions.question: If the orders file changes while a fresh export is being produced, what result should the command use? The sync job is the writer named in `README.md`, while `src/store.js` currently performs one synchronous read.

options.label: Retry latest (Recommended)
options.description: Retry to return the newest complete snapshot; costs another read and must have a bounded retry limit.

options.label: Finish snapshot
options.description: Return the complete snapshot the run started with; it may already be one sync cycle behind when emitted.

options.label: Fail run
options.description: Refuse an ambiguous export so the caller retries; makes transient sync overlap visible as an error.

questions.question: If fresh mode finds `data/orders.json` missing, unreadable, or malformed, should it fail or fall back to cache? Current parsing in `src/store.js` throws, while cached data may be hours old.

options.label: Fail clearly (Recommended)
options.description: Never disguise a broken source as fresh; ad hoc export fails with a diagnostic and produces no CSV.

options.label: Use stale cache
options.description: Keep an export available during sync failures, but a nominally fresh invocation can silently return old data.

leadIn:
The contract now has a fresh-by-default CLI and an explicit `--allow-stale` nightly mode. Fresh runs finish from the complete snapshot they read, even if a newer valid file lands before output, and broken source input fails without CSV.

Verified facts:

- Empty ranges and duplicate orders flow through unchanged in `src/store.js`/`src/exporter.js`; the existing CSV header remains fixed by `test/exporter.test.js`.
- Repeated calls are the intended cache case (`src/cache.js`), and an old cache can be treated as unusable for fresh mode without changing its four-column CSV shape.
- A second reportkit process can write the same cache path; `writeFileSync` currently writes directly to the shared file.
- Cache creation/write errors currently abort the export even after valid rows were loaded.

**Open tension:** cache storage is only an optimization, but the repository does not say whether its failure should suppress otherwise valid fresh CSV. This decides the remaining user-visible failure/recovery behavior; collision-safe cache replacement itself can be implemented without changing the interface.

questions.question: If valid source data was read but updating the disk cache fails, should the export still succeed? Today `writeCache` in `src/cache.js` throws before `src/cli.js` emits CSV.

options.label: Export anyway (Recommended)
options.description: Return valid CSV and treat caching as best-effort; repeated calls may be slower and a warning may be emitted.

options.label: Fail export
options.description: Keep cache health mandatory and emit no CSV; a permission or disk issue blocks finance reporting.

leadIn:
All material decisions are now closed. The user-set probes are:

- Freshness: ad hoc/default runs refresh when `data/orders.json` changes; nightly may explicitly allow stale cache.
- Concurrent upstream rewrite: finish from the complete snapshot already read.
- Failed source input: missing, unreadable, or malformed source fails clearly and emits no CSV.
- Cache-write failure: emit valid CSV anyway, with cache treated as best-effort.

Repository evidence closes the rest: empty/duplicate/range behavior remains in `src/store.js`; CSV order remains protected by `test/exporter.test.js`; cache location and six-hour stale-mode lifetime remain in `src/cache.js`; only the existing CLI/cache seam is extended; no persistent business data or CSV schema migrates.

**Inference:** the smallest compatible implementation is fresh-by-default source-versioned cache validation, `--allow-stale` for the nightly caller, collision-safe best-effort cache writes, and focused CLI/export tests. The implementation and decision record wait only on confirmation of this resolved contract.

questions.question: Proceed with this contract: default exports reflect the source snapshot read for that run; `--allow-stale` permits the existing six-hour cache; source failures emit no CSV; cache-write failures do not block valid CSV; CSV columns and filtering stay unchanged; tests will prove source-change refresh, stale opt-in, snapshot behavior, failures, and column stability. Is anything missing or wrong?

options.label: Proceed (Recommended)
options.description: Implement this bounded contract and its tests; the external nightly script will need to add `--allow-stale`.

options.label: Revise contract
options.description: Pause implementation so you can identify a behavior or scope change first.
